chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated that from al-Nadr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:
I said to Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام: What about the supererogatory prayer on Friday?

He said: Six rak'ahs before the sun's decline, and two rak'ahs at its decline. The recitation in the first is Surat al-Jumu'ah and in the second Surat al-Munafiqun, and after the obligatory prayer there are eight rak'ahs.
Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Acting upon the first narrations is preferable, and that is also indicated by this.

key_terms.الرِّوَايَاتِ الْأُولَى: the earlier narrations which the compiler states are preferable to follow
key_terms.النَّافِلَةُ: the supererogatory prayer performed in addition to the obligatory prayer
key_terms.الْجُمُعَةِ: Surat al-Jumu'ah, recommended for recitation in the first rak'ah here
key_terms.الْفَرِيضَةِ: the obligatory prayer after which eight rak'ahs are performed
key_terms.الْقِرَاءَةُ: the prescribed recitation in the prayer
key_terms.الْمُنَافِقِينَ: Surat al-Munafiqun, recommended for recitation in the second rak'ah here
key_terms.زَوَالِ الشَّمْسِ: the sun's decline from midday, marking a specified prayer time
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ: Friday, the day on which these recommended prayer rulings are being discussed

ai.seo_question: How many nafilah rak'ahs are recommended on Friday and what should be recited in them?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding the nafilah prayers on Friday, specifying their number and timing before and after the obligatory prayer. It also indicates the recommended recitation of Surat al-Jumu'ah and Surat al-Munafiqun in the two rak'ahs at the time of zawal, while the compiler notes that preference is given to the earlier narrations on the matter.
